newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt to draw up sequester if revenues fall.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt to draw up sequester if revenues fall.

text.p: The Russian government will have to present a law on sequestering spending if revenues fall below 90 percent of quarterly budget targets, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.
The clause in the 1997 budget law raises the prospect of political fighting about the budget throughout the year, as officials acknowledge the revenue plan is unrealistic.

Spending cuts must be proportional for all spending items except protected ones, such as defence and social security items, which cannot be touched, macroeconomic department head Anton Siluanov told Reuters.
If revenues are less than 100 percent but more than 90 percent of the target the government can introduce a sequester plan without consulting the Duma, he said.

The International Monetary Fund, which visits Moscow regularly to assess whether to disburse monthly tranches of its $10 billion loan to Russia, takes into consideration a monthly revenue forecast compiled by the Finance Ministry, said Arkady Dvorkovich, an expert with the ministry's Economic Expert Group.
Under the agreement between Russia and the IMF, Russia should collect no less than 90 percent of the forecast monthly revenues to get a new IMF tranche, he said.
The monthly targets have not yet been published as the IMF and Russia have not yet agreed the economic programme for 1997 underlying the loan.

The shortfall in budgeted revenues led the IMF to repeatedly delay tranches of the loan in the second half of last year. Tranches for January and February have not yet been paid out while the fund examines the revenues picture more closely.
